scope_groups.header: Survey - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Perform all calculations and prepare the staking plan for all layout work from the Civil Engineer's CAD background files.
Verify horizontal and vertical control points and provide all control survey work for the entire Project, including 3 GPS control points.
Provide and maintain all onsite control points and benchmarks.
Verify existing tie-in grades match the grading plans, and verify offsite elevations against the Civil Engineer's CAD file.
Notify Contractor of any offsite elevation discrepancies within two weeks of Notice to Proceed.
Provide record as-built survey documentation for all new site wet and dry utilities.
Provide a Project Monument Survey at completion of the Project, as required by the Owner.

scope_groups.header: Layout & Staking - Provide all materials, labor, equipment, and supervision for a complete Scope of Work per plans and specifications. This Scope of Work shall include, but not be limited to:
items: Stake Contractor's staging and parking area corners.
Stake demolition limits and rough grade for all site improvements.
Stake all utility work, including domestic water, irrigation mains and RPPAs, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer systems.
Includes drainage staking for the synthetic turf field, running track, and sand pit systems.
Includes electrical and low voltage ductbanks, vaults, pedestals, transformers, and site lighting, including sports field lighting; coordinate locations with Electrical & Low Voltage Subcontractor.
Coordinate utility staking with Earthwork, Paving, Wet Utilities & Site Demo Subcontractor prior to trenching and installation.
Stake natural gas piping from the meter location and all other known or located underground utilities.
Stake rough grade for building pads at corners and on a 40' minimum grid, including redheads and blue tops.
Provide sawcut limits for all curbs, gutters, and paving to be removed.
Provide Certified Building Pad documentation and Finished Floor monument and elevation certification.
Stake all building grid lines, transferring vertical grid lines to top of footing and slab on grade.
Provide redheads and bluetops for the asphalt running track at 50' intervals, and stake finish grades at the same interval.
Provide final staking for curb and gutter, sidewalks, and flatwork.
Stake rough grade for the entire site at 100' intervals, including grade breaks, angle points, and curb transitions.
Stake all site concrete, including curbs, gutters, sidewalks, and equipment and utility pads.
Stake site amenities, including the running track, synthetic turf field, bleachers, press box, ticket booth, scoreboard poles, and chain link fencing.
Includes staking for track text, lane staggering stripes, track and field event striping, and synthetic turf field logo layout.
Stake athletic equipment, including goal posts, pole vault, high jump, discus and shot put rings and toeboards, discus cage, long jump board, and soccer goals.
Stake sports field lighting and flagpoles.
Include as-built survey monuments as record of survey.
Provide an hourly rate breakdown with the Proposal.
Coordinate staking sequence with Contractor's Preliminary Construction Schedule and Phased Logistics Plan.

Prewitt's Exhibit A item 11 excludes 'As-Built Survey and Drawing Requirements' by name, contradicting the Scope of Work narrative's Survey items f, g, and h (offsite elevation verification, record as-built utility survey, Project Monument Survey). FLAGGED, not adopted -- the exhibit carries the full narrative obligation.

Prewitt's Exhibit A item 6 excludes 'staking for landscaping, hardscape and irrigation,' which contradicts the narrative's own Utility Staking item c.ii, 'Irrigation water mains and RPPA.' FLAGGED, not adopted -- irrigation main/RPPA staking stays in the exhibit's utility-staking item.

Prewitt's Exhibit A item 3 states the survey proposal 'does not reflect staking for the Landscape, Structural, Architectural or Mechanical portion of plans,' which is inconsistent with Prewitt's own priced Final Staking and Building Corner/Grid Line Staking tasks -- both of which explicitly price bleacher ADAs, sport features, scoreboards, flagpole, goal posts, press box (Landscape/Architectural items) and building corner/grid staking (Architectural/Structural). Read as boilerplate inconsistent with their own pricing, not adopted as a scope carve-out.

The Scope of Work narrative's Survey item h reads 'provide Project Monument Survey, as required for City of Las Vegas' -- this project is in Nye County/Tonopah, not the City of Las Vegas, and appears to be leftover boilerplate from a different project template. Rosevear's own proposal silently corrects this to 'as required for NCSD.' The exhibit is drafted 'as required by the Owner' to avoid carrying the wrong jurisdiction forward, but the underlying narrative should be corrected at its source.

Prewitt's commercial terms (Exhibit A items 12-14: entire site assumed available when scheduled with additional mobilizations to be discussed; two-business-day minimum notice to schedule field crews; re-staking after vandalism/damage billed as additional work with a two-hour minimum, per their Prevailing Wage Fee Schedule) are common surveying trade practice but appear nowhere in the Contract Documents. Worth a PM decision on whether re-staking after damage to Contractor-protected stakes is base scope or a priced T&M add -- not adopted here.
